evidence: 0116 (records patients add themselves, text only; Akos handover step 6; owner decision 25 with D7, hide and keep); unsigned until the owner signs. Written on 0103 (34d69557); it reads nothing 0104-0115 add. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: additive only. pg_dump --schema-only of a 0103 database before and after differs by the new table ehr.patient_entries (its primary key, unique key, index, foreign key to identity.patients, three triggers, forced row-level security, two policies and grants), three new functions (ehr.create_my_patient_entry and ehr.withdraw_my_patient_entry, SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE to hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; ehr.patient_entries_guard, granted to no role), their comments, and the source-kind CHECK of ehr.patient_evidence_chunks and ehr.staff_evidence_chunks, which gains patient_entry (written through NOT VALID, then validated). No existing column, row, policy, grant or function body changes. Today's EHR image reads no new object and writes only the 13 chunk kinds the wider CHECK still accepts; the new image touches the new objects only while PATIENT_ENTRIES_ENABLED is on (default off). runtime-grants.sql gains the same grants (SELECT on the table, EXECUTE on the two commands; no write grant). PROOFS on throwaway PostgreSQL 16 clusters (pgvector 0.6.0), synthetic data only: (1) the production chain 0001-0103 (104 files) then 0116 through the runner: plan 1 pending, dry run rolled back with 104 rows kept, applied in 28 ms and 59 ms in two runs, then 0 pending twice; applying the file again refuses 55000 "0116: already applied"; role bootstrap and verify pass; 78 of 78 database suites pass (77 before plus patient-entries). (2) A fresh install of 105 files: dry run, apply, 0 pending, bootstrap, verify, 78 of 78. (3) test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passed: baseline 104, integrated 105, declared [0116_patient_entries.sql], with production's runtime-grants.sql (sha256 594d7835...) as the baseline and again with the git-derived baseline; migrationGrantsMatchRuntimeGrants 2468, rowSecurityUnchanged 185, migrator not superuser and not BYPASSRLS. (4) Non-superuser: on a 0103 copy re-owned to a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, the runner applies it as that role's login and as a member login that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it, and the suite passes on both; a stranger is refused 42501 with nothing applied. (5) Refused with nothing applied (104 rows): a changed platform.reject_mutation or ehr.patient_self_context body, another source-kind CHECK on either chunk table, a chunk table owned by another role, audit_platform_authority disabled; and 55P03 after 5.4 to 6.6 s (the runner's start included) with a write held open on identity.patients or a read held open on either chunk table. (6) Locks held to commit: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.patients; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on both chunk tables (last in the file); none on audit.events or any other existing table. (7) Ten mutants of the file (read policy without the active filter, no patient-self check, a two-way guard, no daily limit, no Lagos date check, created on a reused key, the staff CHECK without patient_entry, withdraw keeping the chunks, a title in the audit, a withdrawn double-tap twin replayed) each fail the suite. Not proven here: a production-sized copy of identity.patients and of the chunk tables (the lock window grows with the chunk tables' validation, measured by the plan's study at 9 ms for 50,000 chunks).
